spec.full_target: Let n,m be positive integers and u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m jointly smooth. Let q be unit. Assume |u|=1, u_tt−Δ_xu=a u, and u=q outside a compact set locally uniformly in time. Define e=|u_t|²+Σ|∂_xj u|² and E=∫e dx. Prove integrability, differentiability and E'=0 for every r>0.
spec.conclusion: For every r>0, e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

propositions.statement: For every r>0, e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

argument.text: Fix r>0 and define J=[r/2,3r/2], a compact interval inside (0,∞) with r interior. H003 supplies C_J. Smoothness and constancy imply derivatives vanish off C_J and at its boundary. Thus e is continuous compactly supported and M001 gives integrability. Choose box B containing C_J. M004 gives uniform continuity of e_t on B×J. M002 represents time difference quotients as averages of e_t, which converge uniformly; finite measure allows integration, giving E'(r)=∫_B e_t.

Differentiate e. For g_j=u_t·u_j, its derivative is (∂_j u_t)·u_j+u_t·u_jj, continuous compactly supported and integrable by M001. Coordinate permutation and M003 give Fubini. M002 on a large interval yields ∫∂_j g_j=0 from endpoint values. Summing gives E'=2∫u_t·(u_tt−Δu). Differentiating H001 gives u·u_t=0; H002 gives acceleration=a u, so integrand vanishes. Thus E'=0. r was arbitrary.
